facts.text: The single most useful structural finding in this synthesis is not stated in any one input report: **the federal statutory definition of a salvage automobile and the insurer's operating total-loss rule are the same inequality, algebraically rearranged.** Four sources that appear to describe different tests describe one test with different terms added to the left-hand side.

The two agencies are not strictly in conflict — one governs first-party claim settlement, the other governs ad valorem property assessment — but they take opposite positions on whether the brand alone is a valid basis for a number. Only New York was checked among claims regulators; whether other states' regulators take the New York position is unknown. **Unresolved.**

Valuation here is not one number but a **comparison of two numbers**. A damaged vehicle has a pre-loss value (what an equivalent undamaged, clean-title unit is worth) and a residual value (what the damaged unit is worth, essentially as parts plus a rebuild option). The cost of restoring the second to the first is the repair estimate.
